findings.title: Memory gate spec-doc contradiction: docs/rust-migration-guide.md:305 still says <10 MiB while amended goal says <40 MiB
findings.description: P2 Done condition in docs/rust-migration-guide.md:305 specifies 'Private Bytes < 10 MiB (软件渲染)'. The session amended G4 goal done_when from <10 MiB to <40 MiB via transition request amend-g4-memory-threshold-chg001 (status: applied). The amendment is honest — self-check SC-09 records the original <10 MiB gate as FAIL (33.66 MiB normal, 37.04 MiB UI_SMOKE, 0/60 below 10 MiB), SC-10 records the <40 MiB fallback as PASS, and the amendment reason documents the bounded optimization failure and unreachability within P2. However, the spec doc was neither superseded nor conflict-marked, leaving a code/spec contradiction: the operative acceptance threshold (<40 MiB) diverges from the documented spec (<10 MiB).
findings.suggested_fix: Route the contradiction per review contract: mark as spec conflict (maestro spec conflict mark) since both thresholds are valid at different scopes (<10 MiB ideal P3 target, <40 MiB P2 reality), then adjudicate via knowledge audit. Do NOT edit the spec in place.

impact.blast_radius: P2 acceptance criteria ambiguity; future reviewers may cite the stale <10 MiB threshold

findings.title: Bounded Tokio current-thread optimization did not reduce memory (+2.5 MiB unexplained delta)
findings.description: Run 010 changed the SSE dedicated thread from new_multi_thread(2) to new_current_thread().enable_all() and narrowed tokio features to rt,sync,time,macros. The bounded optimization attempt is honest — self-check SC-08 records it as FAIL: post-repair UI_SMOKE min 37.039 MiB vs baseline UI_SMOKE min 34.504 MiB under identical measurement condition (release,winit-software,UI_SMOKE). The +2.535 MiB delta is explicitly flagged as 'unproven (no controlled runtime-only A/B performed)'. The optimization is functionally benign (no regression in SSE behavior) but did not achieve its memory-reduction goal. Deeper memory reduction requires P3-era renderer/backend substitution, outside P2 boundary.
findings.suggested_fix: No code fix needed — the optimization is honest and functionally correct. The memory delta is unexplained without a controlled A/B; if memory reduction is required, pursue P3 renderer/backend substitution (deferred per session decisions).

impact.blast_radius: No functional impact; memory optimization goal unmet but honestly recorded

findings.title: panel_after_click Locked->Expanded parity verified exact match against C# FloatingWindowViewModel.cs:258-270
findings.description: panel_after_click at floating_window.rs:92-101 implements Expanded->Locked, Locked->Expanded, Collapsed->no-op, Clickthrough->no-op. This exactly matches C# OnBarClick (FloatingWindowViewModel.cs:258-270): Expanded->Locked, Locked->Expanded, Collapsed not responsive. The Rust impl adds an explicit Clickthrough=>Clickthrough arm (C# implicitly does nothing for Clickthrough in OnBarClick). The 4-variant PanelState enum (Collapsed, Expanded, Locked, Clickthrough) matches C# enum at FloatingWindowViewModel.cs:31. Deterministic test panel_after_click_parity_matches_csharp_locked_expanded_toggle (floating_window.rs:1113-1121) asserts all 4 transitions.

location.code_snippet: pub fn panel_after_click(panel: PanelState) -> PanelState { match panel { PanelState::Expanded => PanelState::Locked, PanelState::Locked => PanelState::Expanded, PanelState::Collapsed => PanelState::Collapsed, PanelState::Clickthrough => PanelState::Clickthrough, } }

findings.title: clamp_rect_to_work_area pure helper correctly clamps unsnapped drag to monitor work area with edge-case coverage
findings.description: clamp_rect_to_work_area (floating_interactions.rs:419-432) is a pure, Win32-agnostic helper that clamps a window rect to the work area. It handles: invalid rects (returns original), oversized windows (left/top align to work_area origin via .max(work_area.left)), offscreen left/right/negative origin. Uses saturating_sub/saturating_add for overflow safety. finish_drag (floating_window.rs:857-885) calls this in the unsnapped branch, only invoking SetWindowPos when clamped position differs from current. Two deterministic tests cover offscreen/negative and oversized/invalid cases. The round_i32 helper (floating_interactions.rs:434-438) clamps to i32 range before casting — prevents UB.

location.code_snippet: pub fn clamp_rect_to_work_area(window: PhysicalRect, work_area: PhysicalRect) -> PhysicalRect { if !window.is_valid() || !work_area.is_valid() { return window; } let max_left = work_area.right.saturating_sub(width).max(work_area.left); ... }

findings.suggested_fix: No fix needed — correct and well-tested.

findings.title: Pinned cards capped ListView with max-visible-pinned and pinned-area-height correctly bounds geometry
findings.description: floating_window.slint:202-203 adds max-visible-pinned (3) and pinned-area-height = min(pinned-processes.length, max-visible-pinned) * 40px. The pinned-list ListView (slint:276-285) uses this capped height. The Shell window height (slint:184) uses min(218px, 96px + pinned-area-height) for collapsed state. The details rectangle (slint:289,291) uses y=92px+pinned-area-height and height=408px-pinned-area-height. This caps the pinned area at 3 cards (120px) with scrollable overflow via ListView. Architecture is clean: pure Slint property binding, no imperative code. Backward-compatible: processes list and details panel geometry consume the capped height.

location.code_snippet: property <int> max-visible-pinned: 3; property <length> pinned-area-height: min(root.pinned-processes.length, root.max-visible-pinned) * 40px;
